candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a common denominator and rewrite one or both fractional parts as equivalent fractions so the quantities are in the same unit before subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same core operation of creating like denominators before subtraction. B and C differ slightly on whether rewriting a whole as 0/n belongs here, but the shared central concept is denominator alignment via equivalent fractions.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract quantities once they are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators of like fractions and subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers when no regrouping is required.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A S02, B S03, and C S03 all cover the direct subtraction step after preparatory rewriting is complete. B and C explicitly mention combining parts into a result, but the underlying cognitive concept is the same direct subtraction of already-aligned quantities.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole or mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as converting an improper mixed number to a standard mixed number or expressing a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B S02 and C S02 both isolate pre-subtraction structural rewriting as its own skill. A does not separate this concept; instead, its S03 combines normalization with borrowing, so A's skill is better aligned elsewhere to preserve one-to-one concept mapping.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup by borrowing one whole and converting it into fractional units when the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A S03 uniquely bundles borrowing/regrouping with normalization, but its distinctive concept not separately represented in B or C is the borrowing action itself. B and C fold borrowing together with simplification rather than isolating it as a standalone skill.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: After or during subtraction, regroup by borrowing from the whole part when needed and reduce the resulting fraction or zero form to lowest terms.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: B S04 and C S04 both combine post-alignment regrouping with simplification into one broader skill. A separates simplification into S04 and includes borrowing inside S03, so no single A skill matches this combined concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce the subtraction result to lowest terms and present it in an appropriate final form such as a fraction, mixed number, or integer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A S04 isolates final reduction and expression as a separate skill. In B and C, simplification is absorbed into broader skills that also include borrowing, so this standalone simplification concept appears only in A.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks share strong agreement on denominator alignment and direct subtraction after alignment. The main divergence is granularity around pre-subtraction rewriting, borrowing, and simplification: A separates simplification and partially separates borrowing, B separates normalization but combines borrowing with simplification, and C similarly separates normalization while combining borrowing and simplification. Every expert skill_id was mapped exactly once, with 3/3 consensus on the two core subtraction workflow skills and lower consensus on the more finely split restructuring and post-subtraction skills.
